verdict.rationale: Lambda documents workspace firewall rules that control incoming traffic, either globally or scoped to individual instances, which is the mechanism for exposing ports. It also references a guide for hosting a load-balanced API server. For private networking, the evidence covers only 1-Click Clusters, with RDMA interconnect between nodes and head nodes used as bastion hosts, not general private networking between instances. Missing for 10: explicit docs on opening or allowing specific ports to serve apps, private networking (VPC/private IPs) between On-Demand instances, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can expose ports to serve applications from my instance and connect instances over private networking

citations.quote: You can restrict incoming traffic to the instances in a workspace, including 1-Click Cluster management (head) nodes, by creating firewall rules on the Firewall page
You can create global rules that apply to all of the instances in the workspace, or rulesets scoped to individual instances and their regions.
Whether you're looking to fine-tune a model or host a load-balanced API server for inference, we have a guide for you.
enabling peer-to-peer GPUDirect RDMA at up to 3200 Gb/s
Each 1CC includes 3x CPU management (head) nodes for use as jump boxes (bastion hosts) and for cluster administration and job scheduling.
